text: From sunrise until the evening steamer horns echoed across the estuary, Erubami pushed his heavy wooden handcart through the narrow streets of Banjul.
He hauled sacks of groundnuts, crates of salted fish, and bolts of Dutch wax prints for the merchants of Albert Market.

His muscles were corded like mangrove roots, and his smile never faltered, though his pocket held scarcely enough copper coins each evening to buy a bowl of coos and smoked bonga for his family in Half-Die.
